publication: David Marker, Lectures on Infinitary Model Theory, Fall 2013. University of Illinois Chicago author PDF.

reviews.checked_passages: §1 printed 4–7: well-founded infinitary syntax, finite common free-variable context, semantics and Example 1.5 compactness boundary.
reviews.consumers: Infinitary logic: finite-context countable connectives, ordinary-syntax embedding, infinity and standard successor, explicit finite-model compactness counterexample.
reviews.outcome: No serious defect adopted. The entry states its L_{omega1,omega} convention explicitly and proves the selected claims locally; it avoids extending this review to later equivalence-notation slips, exercises, Scott analysis or advanced model theory.

reviews.checked_passages: Section2.2: definitions of ordinal back-and-forth formulas, Lemmas2.13 and2.15 and their proofs, the Scott-sentence construction and Theorem2.19 proof; PDF pages15–18 (one-based). The adjacent group-theoretic corollary and later descriptive-set-theory material are excluded.
reviews.consumers: First-four-foundational-area gap audit; proposed coverage only, with no new entry adoption.
reviews.outcome: Countable-vocabulary, countable-structure Scott sentences need only the existing infinitary syntax, transfinite recursion and back-and-forth machinery. Restricting to that scope avoids an unstated bound on arbitrary vocabularies. MARKER-SCOTT-01 records two local witness-domain slips in the inspected proofs. No Scott entry is adopted here.

reviews.checked_passages: Execution selection reconfirms the previously assessed section2.2 definitions and Lemmas2.13,2.15 plus the full Scott-sentence construction/Theorem2.19, PDFpp15–18. No group-theoretic corollary or descriptive-set-theory application.
reviews.consumers: Root eight-entry execution plan: Scott sentences for countable structures.
reviews.outcome: Apply MARKER-SCOTT-01 witness-domain repairs. Restrict the signature and fixed nonempty structure to countable, construct actual finite-context countable infinitary formulas at countable ordinals, prove countable stabilization and the forth/back system, then countable isomorphism. The finite-structure case and possible uncountable models of a Scott sentence are explicit boundaries; no full Scott-rank spectrum is adopted.

reviews.checked_passages: Adoption reuses section2.2 PDFpp15–18, ordinal comparison formulas and the full Lemmas2.13/2.15 and Theorem2.19 proofs; MARKER-SCOTT-01 is repaired.
reviews.consumers: scott-sentences-for-countable-structures. Adopted blocks are recorded in entry_refs.
reviews.outcome: The entry uses countable vocabulary and a fixed nonempty countable structure, includes all finite terms, constructs actual finite-context countable infinitary comparison formulas, proves countable stabilization inside the fixed structure and the specified Scott sentence. Models of that sentence supply an actual back-and-forth system. Countable isomorphism includes finite carriers; the infinity example explains that uncountable models are allowed.
